speaker: Doctor
text: To better understand your symptoms, could you tell me when the leg weakness and unsteady gait first began? Also, have you noticed any changes in your vision or speech?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any recent head trauma, or noticed a new headache or fever? I also need to know if you have a history of substance use or any recent infections. REQUEST TEST: Brain MRI

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain: Disseminated, nonenhancing white matter lesions with no mass effect.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the MRI findings of disseminated, nonenhancing white matter lesions combined with your cognitive decline and paranoia, I need to rule out infectious or inflammatory causes. Do you have a history of HIV or other immunocompromising conditions? REQUEST TEST: Lumbar_Puncture

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal CSF findings ruling out active infection or inflammation, these nonenhancing white matter lesions strongly suggest a vascular etiology like multiple infarcts. Do you have any history of hypertension, diabetes, or high cholesterol? REQUEST TEST: Carotid Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: Since vascular and infectious causes are effectively ruled out, I need to consider toxic or metabolic etiologies for these white matter changes. Have you been exposed to any industrial solvents, or do you have a history of heavy alcohol use or chronic drug abuse? REQUEST TEST: Serum_B12_and_Folate

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Serum B12: 80 pg/mL, Serum Folate: 2.0 ng/mL

speaker: Doctor
text: Your significantly low B12 and folate levels explain the white matter lesions, cognitive decline, and neurological deficits. DIAGNOSIS READY: Vitamin B12 Deficiency
